items.title: How Raised Earnings Guidance At Textron (TXT) Has Changed Its Investment Story
items.summary: Textron reported third quarter 2026 revenue of US$3,751 million and net income of US$270 million, then raised full year GAAP EPS guidance to a range of US$5.64 to US$5.74 and updated expected income from continuing operations to US$985 million to US$1,000 million. The company combined higher earnings guidance with capital return and funding moves, including a US$521.89 million buyback completed under its February 2026 program and a US$349.3035 million fixed rate bond offering of 5.500% notes...

items.title: GE Aerospace Trades Above 50-Day and 200-Day SMA: Time to Buy?
items.summary: GE trades above its 50-day and 200-day moving averages as strong engine demand, defense contracts and rising earnings estimates fuel its growth momentum.

items.title: Does Textron (TXT) Have Enough Cash Flow To Support Its Price?
items.summary: Textron has delivered a 14.5% share price gain over the past five years. With recent news around aircraft programs and portfolio changes, investors are increasingly asking whether the current US$85.94 price is supported by the cash the business can generate. The 14.5% return over five years puts real weight on the question of whether Textron's current valuation matches the cash flows that have funded that journey so far and are expected ahead.
